basis: GABA catabolic disorder; neurodevelopmental impairment, seizures and other CNS dysfunction affect most patients across the principal subtypes.
Psychogenic sexual dysfunction confined to the reproductive system; no qualifying organ axis.
Progressive cerebellar degeneration; nystagmus, diplopia and dysphagia reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than direct ocular or gastrointestinal damage.
Thoracic skeletal dysplasia with restrictive respiratory dysfunction; kidney failure and cataract each reported in 1/1 patient. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic damage.
Acute intestinal dysfunction; infectious causation is not established for the entire concept.
GnRH deficiency and congenital olfactory dysfunction define the syndrome; reduced bone mineral density occurs in 30-79%. Renal and hearing abnormalities occur in <30%.
Degeneration of the cerebellum; autoimmune mechanisms apply only to a subset of this etiologically heterogeneous group.
Defining osteopenia with fractures, severe myopia and sensorineural hearing loss; intellectual disability in both reported brothers. Enamel hypoplasia omitted because of the cap.
Severe neonatal hyperparathyroidism and hypercalcemia; skeletal demineralization with fractures occurs in 80-99%. Visceral enlargement alone does not establish organ damage.
Inherited beta-globin synthesis disorder causing microcytic anemia; skeletal changes and iron-related organ injury do not apply across major, intermedia and minor forms.
Lipoate biosynthesis defect with hyperglycinemia and progressive spastic CNS disease; optic atrophy and visual impairment occur in 30-79%. Cardiac hypertrophy is very rare.
Umbrella for congenital multiple joint contracture syndromes; neurologic and other organ abnormalities vary by subtype.
Hereditary Wilms tumor subtype; nephroblastoma is a primary renal neoplasm, reported in 5/5 patients.
Inherited epidermal barrier disorder with peeling, scaling and dermatitis; associated atopic dermatitis does not establish a separate systemic immune disorder.
Neurodevelopmental impairment defines the deletion syndrome; strabismus occurs in 80-99%. Epicanthal folds and palmar creases alone do not establish additional organ damage.
Acute necrosis of the renal papillae; no additional organ involvement is intrinsic to the concept.
Spontaneous dissection directly damages a coronary artery; associated myocardial ischemia remains within the cardiovascular axis.
Congenital structural malformation of the tricuspid valve; additional organ injury is not shared across the group.
Bacterial invasion and inflammation cause intestinal wall necrosis. Blood-count and electrolyte changes do not establish direct organ damage; sepsis and DIC occur in <30%.
Developmental malformation of the cerebral cortex with abnormal neurons, epilepsy and possible cognitive impairment.
Congenital skeletal myopathy; ventilation is required in ~80% because of respiratory muscle weakness, without established direct lung damage. Pneumonia is a separate disease.
Benign or malignant neoplasm arising in the colon; lymphoma is only one subtype, and distant organ involvement is not intrinsic to the umbrella.
Defining limb malformations and congenital nasal alar/columellar hypoplasia; nose falls within the pulmonary axis. Neurologic abnormalities occur in <30%.
Sialic acid metabolic/storage disorder; neurodevelopmental impairment is common (>30%) across principal forms. Visceral enlargement alone does not establish organ damage.
Inherited lipoate biosynthesis disorder; encephalopathy, developmental impairment or progressive motor pathway damage affects most patients across the principal subtypes.
